root_cause.text: When reregistering a memory region with only IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS (without IB_MR_REREG_TRANS) to change access from read-only to read-write, the kernel failed to verify that the underlying user memory was pinned as writable, allowing a user to upgrade access without having appropriate page pin permissions, potentially leading to memory corruption or unauthorized writes.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "If IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS changes from RO to RW then the umem has to be re-evaluated to ensure it is properly pinned as RW." The patch introduces `ib_umem_check_rereg()` which returns -EACCES when `(flags & IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS) && !(flags & IB_MR_REREG_TRANS)` and `ib_access_writable(new_access_flags) && !umem->writable`. The fix references commit b40656aa7d55 ("RDMA/umem: remove FOLL_FORCE usage"), indicating that the removal of FOLL_FORCE made this check necessary to enforce correct page pinning.

This conditional only updates access flags when IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS is not set; when the flag is set, the else path updates access flags from user input without checking if the underlying umem supports write, allowing a user to change access to write-capable without verifying writable pinning.
